mission_09: SMAPE uses (|actual| + |predicted|) / 2 as the denominator, which is symmetric and handles cases where actual values are near zero.
MASE scales the forecast MAE by the mean absolute difference of the training data, so values below 1 indicate the forecast beats the naive method.
The Diebold-Mariano test uses a Newey-West heteroskedasticity-and-autocorrelation-consistent variance estimator for the loss differential.
